data.why: The repository ships its own curated, validated dataset (data/concepts.json, data/edges.json, data/paragraphs.json, data/themes.json) which app.py reads directly from the repo's data/ directory; there is no upload feature to exercise.

goals: Begin from a curated starting concept within an editorial theme and progressively reveal one-hop semantic relationships to trace how an idea connects to others in the Monadology
Cross-reference revealed concepts against the canonical Latta translation paragraphs to see how editorial concepts map onto Leibniz's original text
Search for a specific concept or paragraph (by number or §form) and jump directly to it to inspect its connections
Switch between editorial themes to compare how different thematic regions of the text (e.g. nature of monads vs. creation and harmony) are structured
Inspect the full curated graph to assess structural patterns such as connected components, highly connected concepts, and overall relationship density
Read paragraphs sequentially (previous/next) while keeping track of which nodes and relationships have been discovered so far

review.summary: The tree states the tool's purpose, reading Leibniz through both a growing concept graph and the canonical text, at the right depth, and the six cited screens plus the independent replay back it up. It needs small fixes before filing: add the paragraph hover-text preview and the theme-colour reading of the full graph, move the failed graph-click action out of t2, and correct how Fit to screen is described.
